Photograph: Kacper Pempel/Reuters Poland Russian plot to kill Ukrainian American thwarted in Warsaw, says Polish PM Donald Tusk says it is first time ‘someone on the order of Russia’ has sought to attack US citizen in Nato country Associated Press Thu 13 Aug 2026 15.32 EDT Last modified on Thu 13 Aug 2026 18.19 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A Russian plan to kill a Ukrainian American citizen in Warsaw was thwarted by Poland before it could be carried out, the Polish prime minister has said. Donald Tusk said it was the first time that “someone on the order of Russia” had sought to attack a US citizen on the territory of another Nato country. Western officials have previously warned that Russia stepped up a campaign of targeted killings since Vladimir Putin’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine, saying they had disrupted several plots across Europe. But Tusk said this incident was unprecedented. The suspect, who was allegedly recruited by Russia’s secret services, was detained by Polish authorities on 7 August. He will be held in custody for three months, the Warsaw police said in a statement. The American Ukrainian citizen “was uncomfortable for the Putin regime”, Tusk said in a news conference, without elaborating. The operation was carried out in cooperation with US services, said Tomasz Siemoniak, Poland’s minister overseeing intelligence services. He said the targeted victim was a US citizen “of Ukrainian origin”. Officials did not immediately provide further details. The Russian foreign ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The US state department said it was aware of the reports but said it had no additional information. Russia has long been accused of targeting its enemies abroad, including by using rare poisons. But intelligence officials previously told the Associated Press that Russia’s security services are now more brazen in their choice of targets, going after Russian activists and foreign supporters of Ukraine as well as military defectors. Tusk said: “We must assume that the Putin regime will try to eliminate people who are inconvenient for various reasons, in various places around the world.” He added that Poland and other countries must be prepared to counter such actions. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to This is Europe The most pressing stories and debates for Europeans – from identity to economics to the environment after newsletter promotion A bungled bomb plot in Poland exposed a spy – but whose spy was he? Read more Western officials see the campaign as connected to Russia’s broader efforts to undermine European countries that support Ukraine. The AP has mapped about 200 acts of sabotage, arson and other disruption across Europe since the start of the war in Ukraine that officials have linked to Russia. Putin told the AP in June that Russia was not waging a sabotage campaign against Europe. In 2006, British authorities accused Russia of being behind the killing in London of the former FSB officer Alexander Litvinenko with radioactive polonium. The UK also blames Russia for the attempted killing of the former Russian military intelligence officer Sergei Skripal in Salisbury in 2018 with the nerve agent novichok. German authorities said Russia had organised the 2019 killing of Zelimkhan Khangoshvili , a former Chechen rebel commander who was shot in a Berlin park by Vadim Krasikov, a hitman who was later greeted by Putin after he was exchanged in a spy swap. In June, a Russian artist who was critical of Putin was shot and killed at close range near his home in eastern Poland. Tusk said at the time that the killing of Robert Kuzovkov , known by the pseudonym Semyon Skrepetsky, had the hallmarks of a political assassination. He suggested it was possible Russia was behind it but Polish officials have not yet attributed it to Moscow. Last year French officials disrupted a plot that they believe was aimed at killing Vladimir Osechkin, a Russian exile who lives under police protection and works to help military defectors flee Putin’s war. Lithuanian officials also disrupted a plot last year to kill a Lithuanian supporter of Ukraine and another against a Russian activist. Officials in Germany have similarly broken up two plots: one to target the head of a German weapons company supplying Ukraine, the other against a Ukrainian military official. Polish authorities arrested a man in 2024 in what they said was a plot to assassinate the Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy. That year, a Russian helicopter pilot who defected was killed in Spain – Russian operatives were the prime suspects. “This campaign is not by accident or chance,” a senior European intelligence official previously told the AP. “There is political authorisation.” Explore more on these topics Poland Russia Vladimir Putin Donald Tusk Europe Nato Ukraine news Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed World Europe US news Americas Asia Australia Middle East Africa Inequality Global development

Photograph: Rich Pedroncelli/AP US news FBI raids Eric Swalwell’s home amid sexual assault claims inquiry – report Federal agents also ‘seized electronic devices’ from former Democratic representative at San Francisco airport Victoria Bekiempis Thu 20 Aug 2026 14.10 EDT Last modified on Thu 20 Aug 2026 14.11 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Authorities are said to have searched the Washington DC home of disgraced former California Democratic representative Eric Swalwell on Sunday amid an ongoing law enforcement investigation into sexual assault allegations. CNN reported that federal agents on Saturday “seized electronic devices” from Swalwell at the San Francisco airport, citing unnamed sources familiar with the investigation. Multiple other outlets have confirmed the federal search; the Daily Mail was the first to repor t this law enforcement activity. Attorneys who have represented Swalwell could not immediately be reached for comment. Swalwell has denied allegations of sexual assault. Swalwell resigned from Congress following multiple allegations of sexual assault and misconduct that thwarted his campaign for governor. Before stepping down, Swalwell faced extensive bipartisan demands for him to resign or face an expulsion vote. “I am deeply sorry to my family, staff, and constituents for mistakes in judgment I’ve made in my past,” Swalwell said in a statement posted to social media in April. “I will fight the serious false allegation made against me. However, I must take responsibility and ownership for the mistakes I did make.” “Expelling anyone in Congress without due process, within days of an allegation being made, is wrong,” Swalwell had said, in reference to potential removal from office. “But it’s also wrong for my constituents to have me distracted from my duties. Therefore, I plan to resign my seat in Congress.” Swalwell’s resignation came after the US House ethics committee said they had launched an investigation into him. This bipartisan committee announced it would investigate “allegations that [Swalwell] may have engaged in sexual misconduct, including towards an employee working under his supervision”. CBS noted this investigation ended when Swalwell resigned, as the ethics committee “only has jurisdiction over current members and staff”. The US Department of Justice opened an investigation into the disgraced legislator following his resignation, a source previously told the Guardian. Swalwell’s descent from gubernatorial frontrunner to investigative target started in April. The San Francisco Chronicle published an account from an unnamed ex-staffer, who alleged that he sexually assaulted her. CNN also had a similar report which featured allegations from three other women who claimed that Swalwell had sent them unwanted explicit text messages or photos. Asked about the search, the FBI declined to comment. The justice department did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The White House on Monday disclosed de-classified documents on an FBI investigation into Swalwell’s purported relationship with a possible spy more than 10 years ago. The FBI director, Kash Patel, had been reportedly pushing for the disclosure of files in this investigation, CBS News also reported. Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Explanation: Recorded the night of August 12-13, images from four dedicated meteor-monitoring cameras at an astronomical observatory in Czechia were aligned and combined to create this all-night, all-sky view. On that night , the total count came to 1,706 meteors. And since that coincided with the peak activity of the 2026 Perseid Meteor Shower , most are perseids. Their overwhelming numbers make them easy to spot. Quite convincingly, perseid trails all trace back to a single radiant on the sky at the upper right, a region in the annual shower's eponymous constellation Perseus. But meteors belonging to other much less active showers can be revealed by finding their radiants too. For example, seen crossing the perseid trails are meteors from a shower whose radiant lies in Cygnus, known as Kappa Cygnids . The antihelion complex , a general region near Aquarius and opposite the Sun in the sky, is also identifiable as a weak source for meteors. https://www.ibtimes.co.uk/andrew-tate-le.text: Andrew Tate announced plans on 17 September to take legal action against FDC Miami, calling his confinement 'cruel and unusual punishment'.Writing on X, he alleged that his cell lacked hot water and air conditioning and was infested with cockroaches.Tate and his brother Tristan have been detained since July 2026 while fighting extradition to the UK over 59 criminal charges, including rape and human trafficking for sexual exploitation.The brothers deny the criminal allegations against them. Tate says his proposed legal action seeks the same treatment afforded to other prisoners.Andrew Tate Describes Conditions Inside the Unit'I have been left with no choice but to take legal action against FDC Miami for the conditions of my confinement. This is a civil rights issue,' Tate wrote.'I do not ask for special treatment. I asked to be treated the same as any other prisoner and American citizen,' he added.Tate claimed he had been 'downgraded by 95% from what normal prisoners receive'. He presented the figure as his assessment, without a calculation appearing in the quoted statement.Tate said he had spent 61 days in the Special Housing Unit, which he described as a punitive unit for inmates who attack prisoners or guards. He alleged that men who had stabbed fellow inmates were allowed to leave the unit after seven days.On 17 September, he said, staff moved him to another cell within the same unit. The move made his conditions worse, according to his account. He claimed there were '10/15 visible roaches on the ceiling and walls at any one time'.'I have stone-cold water and filth. That's it. NOTHING else,' he wrote.He described his situation as deteriorating and suggested that his treatment was deliberate.FDC Miami Faced Complaints Before Andrew TateOther detainees had raised concerns about FDC Miami before Tate's statement.In July 2026, wives of immigrant detainees shared recorded conversations with their husbands with WLRN. The men described conditions inside the facility, with detainee Cervelo Trujillo reportedly saying, 'Animals get treated better than this.'Human Rights Watch had also documented concerns in a July 2025 report, citing 'extreme overcrowding, unsanitary conditions, and abusive treatment'. It described verbal harassment and humiliation, including invasive cavity searches.Those accounts concern the same facility, but do not independently establish the circumstances Tate described in his cell or his allegations about individual staff members.Andrew Tate Seeks Accounts From Other DetaineesTate also accused a senior staff member of handcuffing him and Tristan during recreation two weeks before his statement and shouting at them over extra books in their cell.'He lost his mind over books. I've never seen a man so angry, over a book,' Tate wrote.He said staff and guards had shown him no respect, despite his efforts to be polite and kind. His attempt to raise concerns with the senior staff member, he alleged, received a dismissive response.Other staff, Tate claimed, had apologised for his living conditions and told him he was the only high-profile prisoner they had seen treated in this manner.A Federal Bureau of Prisons spokesperson stated that the agency does not discuss individual inmates' confinement conditions for privacy, safety and security reasons. The spokesperson said FDC Miami operates in accordance with applicable federal regulations, policies and procedures.The brothers were detained in Romania in 2022 on rape and human trafficking allegations. He also claimed he had been treated better while imprisoned in Romania. A judge rejected their bid for bail earlier in September, leaving them in custody while the UK seeks their extradition.Tate said he had prepared a package detailing 'every single infraction I have witnessed in this facility'. His statement outlined plans for legal action. No court filing or hearing date was cited to establish that proceedings had begun.He asked people who had experienced similar treatment at FDC Miami to contact his team with their own accounts.

Photograph: Mateusz Słodkowski/Zuma Press Wire/Rex/Shutterstock Revolut Millions unable to use Revolut app or cards as company suffers ‘service disruption’ UK banking company insists customers’ funds and data are safe despite problems with sign-in, card payments, transfers and withdrawals Business live – latest updates Julia Kollewe Tue 20 Oct 2026 05.45 EDT Last modified on Tue 20 Oct 2026 05.46 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Revolut customers have been unable to access their money after the banking app went down, affecting a number of services including card payments, cash withdrawals and transfers. The UK banking company said its app was down because of a “service disruption” affecting several services, but insisted that customers’ funds and data were safe. Revolut said its services were currently “partially unavailable”, with problems affecting its sign-up, sign-in, card payments, transfers, ATM withdrawals and cryptocurrency services. Revolut users reported error alerts when they tried to check their accounts. When opening the app, they received a “something went wrong” message, instructing them to “try again later”, and leaving them unable to access their funds. In a statement, Revolut said: “We are currently experiencing a service disruption affecting multiple services. We can confirm that all our customers’ money and data are safe. We’ve been working to fix the issue since it was identified this morning and apologise to anyone affected and for any inconvenience caused.” Revolut is not the only company experiencing problems. Its outage could be linked to issues with Google’s cloud services. The two companies have a strategic partnership , under which Revolut uses Google Cloud’s scalable infrastructure to operate its services. Several fintech companies have been affected after Google reported that “multiple Google Cloud services are experiencing elevated errors and intermittent network failures in europe-west2 region,” adding that it did not have a workaround.
